item.text: The Independent Commission Against Corruption evaluated SAFECOM, the Country Fire Service, Metropolitan Fire Service and State Emergency Service to help prevent corruption arising from conflicts of interest.
item.support:
to prevent or minimise corruption arising from conflicts of 
interests.

item.text: The evaluation examined how policies and procedures for managing conflicts of interest were developed, reviewed, communicated and enforced.
item.support:
The evaluation examined the policies and procedures of SAFECOM that apply to the 
CFS, MFS and SES in respect of the management of conflicts of interests.

item.text: The Commission acknowledged improvements across all four agencies, including their adoption of a common policy for disclosing and managing conflicts.
item.support:
including endorsing a generally sound 
Conflict of Interest and Disclosure Policy which applies uniformly across the sector.

item.text: However, the Commission concluded that none of the agencies complied with that policy and that it was not effectively implemented or enforced.
item.support:
This Policy is not 
effectively implemented or enforced. None of the agencies are compliant with the Policy.

item.text: The Commission also found gaps in written communication and training for staff, volunteers and contractors.
item.support:
Overall, there is a lack of written communication and training materials available to staff, 
volunteers and contractors in all agencies about conflicts of interests.

item.text: It made 25 recommendations covering policies and procedures, communication, training, monitoring and compliance in managing conflicts of interest.
item.support:
The Commission has made twenty-five recommendations to strengthen policies and 
procedures, communication, training, monitoring and compliance relating to conflicts 
of interests.

item.quote:
The emergency services sector lacks consistent, clear and adequate guidance regarding 
the identification, disclosure and management of conflicts of interests.

The nature of induction and other training materials available to staff, volunteers and 
contractors in all agencies about their obligations to identify and disclose conflicts of 
interests requires improvement.

Only the MFS has a general conflict of interests disclosure form for employees to 
complete if they identify that they have any conflicts related to their work.

All four emergency services agencies have taken positive steps in recent years to 
improve management of conflicts of interests, including endorsing a generally sound 
Conflict of Interest and Disclosure Policy which applies uniformly across the sector.
